channel.title: Worcester Business Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Worcester Business Journal (wbjournal.com)

item.title: Mass. business confidence continued to slip in January
item.description: Massachusetts’ business confidence dropped slightly in January as business owners maintained worries about tariffs, federal immigration enforcement, and the cost of running their companies.

item.title: New Worcester conference to promote inclusive leadership
item.description: A new conference on inclusive leadership is coming to Worcester.

item.title: 🔒 Hanscom Federal Credit Union to merge with Western Mass. firm
item.description: Upon being approved by regulators, the merger would see the combined entities operated under the Hanscom Federal Credit Union name.

item.title: WPS and Assumption University launch scholarship, fellowship program
item.description: With the partnership, known as Worcester Together, Assumption will offer scholarships to every WPS student admitted to the university for the 2026-27 and 2027-28 school years.

item.title: 🔒 Former Sunnyside Auto properties in Holden to be redeveloped after $2M sale
item.description: Real estate used by Sunnyside was put on the market in February 2025.

item.title: Health Policy Commission: Health insurers denied 20% of claims in 2024
item.description: Commercial insurers denied roughly one out of every five claims submitted in 2024, with administrative issues driving a large chunk of those blocked coverage requests, according to a new analysis from state health policy officials.

item.title: Nine Central Mass. firms named to Newsweek’s America’s Greatest Workplaces for Women list
item.description: Fifty-six Massachusetts businesses made it onto the magazine’s list of 1,000 U.S. companies.

item.title: MassVentures opens applications for small business grants up to $500K
item.description: Offering between $100,000 and $500,000, START grants support the commercialization efforts of small Massachusetts companies.

item.title: Goldberg, 15 other state treasurers write letter to Trump criticizing economic impact of ICE raids
item.description: The letter from 16 Democrat state fiscal officers did not ask Trump to stop his administration's immigration crackdown, but instead to "immediately scale back enforcement activities."

item.title: 🔒 Worcester developer expands further by buying 10 apartment buildings for $8.5M
item.description: Ermani purchased the properties from Pars Realty, a Holden-based firm managed by Christina Papalilo.
